correctness.rationale: For every binary field q=2^m, m>=3, the proof normalizes the ordered six-tuple by the sharply triply transitive conic PGL2 action, computes its Pascal-line quadratic, and counts its rational roots using four proved mutually disjoint parameter exclusions. The two nonlinear exclusion loci have explicit birational parametrizations; their only field-dependence is the number rho_q of roots of k^2+k+1. Dividing total normalized counts by line-orbit sizes and twelve ordered descriptions gives all three exact multiplicities and sharp positivity. A separate direct projective enumeration reproduces all 73 and 273 line fibers at q=8,16; normalized exceptional counts agree for q=8,16,32,64,128,256. The infinitely many other q follow from the symbolic proof, not the tests.

value.rationale: Pascal-line fibers are a natural invariant of a smooth conic and the rational six-point configurations over finite fields. In characteristic two the conic nucleus makes the tangent case structurally distinct, and the count exhibits an additional finite-subfield root correction arising from an explicit singular cubic. The theorem is a complete natural fiber classification for all binary extensions, with a sharp q=8 all-line-surjectivity threshold; it supplies a nontrivial excluded-boundary result rather than an arbitrary finite census.
